conventions: galah + et + ozen + 1cs suffix ('uncover my ear') rendered 'disclose(th) to/unto me': the verb and ozen share one unit under rule 30 headed on the verb (with any supplied relative or auxiliary, 'that discloseth', 'did disclose'); the object marker takes the 'to'/'unto' the recast verb needs to reach its object under rule 16; the suffix takes 'me'; a supplied object 'it' (22.17) is added under rule 44. Applied at 22.8 (twice) and 22.17.

ka-yyom ha-zzeh -> 'as at this day': the kaf takes 'as at' whole as one rendering headed on 'as' (alternative: 'at' added), the assimilated article and the agreement article are unrepresented, and zeh takes 'this' under rule 41. Applied at 22.8 and 22.13.

sha'al lo b-YHWH/b-Elohim -> 'inquire of Jehovah/God for him': the bet takes 'of', the lamed takes 'for' and its suffix 'him'. Applied at 22.10, 22.13 and 22.15; le-'orev -> 'to lie in wait' gives 'to' to the lamed and 'lie in wait' to the participle headed on 'wait' (alternative head 'lie') at 22.8 and 22.13.
report: Read all 23 verses end to end against the candidate table. Every multi-treatment bucket is the ASV rendering one word differently (waw as And/Then/therefore/now/with/who/or/But; lamed as to/for/of/unto or silent before a bare object; kol as all/every/every one) and none is a split.

Constructions repeated across verses are analysed identically: galah et-ozen -> 'disclose(th)' fused with the marker taking 'to/unto' (22.8 x2, 22.17); ka-yyom ha-zzeh -> 'as at this day' with both articles unrepresented (22.8, 22.13); sha'al lo b- -> 'inquire of ... for him' (22.10, 22.13, 22.15); le-'orev -> 'to lie in wait' headed on 'wait' (22.8, 22.13); ba-yyom ha-hu -> 'on that day' (22.18, 22.22); beit avi -> possessive 'father's house' (22.1, 22.11, 22.16, 22.22) against 'the house of my father' in 22.15 where the ASV writes 'of'; nitsav al -> 'stood about/by him' (22.6, 22.7, 22.9, 22.17); mi-sham -> 'thence' fused (22.1, 22.3).

The four added units (22.1 'it', 22.3 'and be', 22.17 'it', 22.22 'the death') are supplied objects or a supplied clause the Hebrew does not write; each note names the alternative and none contradicts another verse.

BSB disagreements are all convention: unrendered apodosis/relative/circumstantial waws (22.1, 22.9, 22.20), a resumptive suffix the relative already carries (22.2), silent datives and purpose lameds (rule 40), articles on demonstrative phrases and the proper name Gibeah/Ramah, and paragogic he (22.15, 22.23). No genuine error found.
Nothing here generalises beyond what the contract already says; no promotion or amendment.
